}} '''Justin Aaron Jackson''' (born March 28, 1995) is an American former professional [[basketball]] player who last played for the [[Texas Legends]] of the [[NBA G League]]. Jackson took part in the [[2014 McDonald's All-American Boys Game]] and was named its co-MVP, along with [[Jahlil Okafor]]. He played [[college basketball]] for the [[North Carolina Tar Heels men's basketball|North Carolina Tar Heels]] from 2015 to 2017. In 2017, Jackson was named a consensus first-team All-American and won an NCAA championship as a member of the Tar Heels. A [[small forward]], Jackson was chosen by the [[Portland Trail Blazers]] as the fifteenth overall pick in the [[2017 NBA draft]] before being traded to the [[Sacramento Kings]] on draft night. As of August 2023, Jackson had played for the Kings, the [[Dallas Mavericks]], the [[Oklahoma City Thunder]], the [[Milwaukee Bucks]], the [[Boston Celtics]], and the [[Phoenix Suns]] over the course of his six-year NBA career. He won an NBA championship with the Bucks in 2021. Jackson has also played for the [[Stockton Kings]] and the [[Texas Legends]] of the [[NBA G League]]. ==High school career== [[File:20140402 MCDAAG MVPs (2).JPG|thumb|left|upright|Jackson and [[2014 McDonald's All-American Boys Game]] co-MVP [[Jahlil Okafor]]]] Jackson played [[basketball]] for Homeschool Christian Youth Association (HCYA), a nonprofit Christian service organization created to serve home school families and students in [[Houston]] and the surrounding area.{{cite news|title=The life of Justin Jackson|url=http://usatodayhss.com/2013/the-life-of-justin-jackson|access-date=April 19, 2017|work=[[USA Today]]|date=December 10, 2013}} He led the Warriors to a national championship in the 2012 season, and won the Sullivan Award, which is awarded to the top homeschool basketball player of the year. He continued to shine in his final year, averaging 31.5 points and 9.1 rebounds in his successful last season.{{cite web|title=Justin Jackson Bio|url=http://www.goheels.com/ViewArticle.dbml?DB_OEM_ID=3350&ATCLID=209532765|website=GoHeels.com|access-date=July 16, 2014|archive-date=July 26, 2014|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140726071320/http://www.goheels.com/ViewArticle.dbml?DB_OEM_ID=3350&ATCLID=209532765|url-status=dead}} Jackson became known as one of the most potent [[high school]] athletes in the nation which promptly triggered a highly publicized recruitment. He was given offers by [[Baylor Bears basketball|Baylor]], [[Georgetown Hoyas men's basketball|Georgetown]], [[Maryland Terrapins men's basketball|Maryland]], [[North Carolina Tar Heels men's basketball|North Carolina]], [[Ohio State Buckeyes men's basketball|Ohio State]], [[Oklahoma Sooners men's basketball|Oklahoma]], [[Oklahoma State Cowboys basketball|Oklahoma State]], [[Texas Longhorns men's basketball|Texas]], [[Texas A&M Aggies men's basketball|Texas A&M]], [[Virginia Cavaliers men's basketball|Virginia]], [[Virginia Tech Hokies men's basketball|Virginia Tech]], and [[Washington Huskies men's basketball|Washington]]. Jackson was rated a five-star recruit by [[Rivals.com]], [[ESPN]], and [[247Sports.com]]. Eventually, the [[small forward]] signed with North Carolina. He was marked as one of the top players in the Class of 2014.{{cite web|title=Justin Jackson|url=https://sports.yahoo.com/footballrecruiting/basketball/recruiting/player-Justin-Jackson-113617|publisher=Yahoo!|access-date=July 16, 2014}}{{cite web|title=Justin Jackson|url=https://www.espn.com/college-sports/basketball/recruiting/player/_/id/102457/justin-jackson|publisher=ESPN|access-date=July 16, 2014}}{{cite web|title=Justin Jackson|url=https://247sports.com/Player/Justin-Jackson-14192|website=247Sports.com|access-date=July 16, 2014}} Following his years with HCYA, Jackson was named to the [[2014 McDonald's All-American Boys Game]] on January 29, 2014. After scoring the first few points of the game, the [[North Carolina Tar Heels men's basketball|North Carolina]] recruit was named co-MVP with [[Jahlil Okafor]]. Jackson ended with 23 points off 11-of-12 shooting, making him the game's top scorer. He also won the Jack Daly Award for sportsmanship.{{cite magazine|last1=Johnson|first1=Chris|title=2014 McDonald's All-American game: Okafor, Jackson take home MVP honors|url=https://www.si.com/college-basketball/one-and-one/2014/04/03/mcdonalds-all-american-game-jahlil-okafor-justin-jackson|magazine=Sports Illustrated|date=April 3, 2014 |access-date=July 16, 2014}} ==College career== In his freshman season, Jackson was selected to the ACC All-Freshman team and helped his team reach the championship of the [[2015 ACC men's basketball tournament|2015 ACC tournament]]. In his sophomore season, Jackson helped his team win the [[2016 ACC men's basketball tournament|2016 ACC tournament]] and reach the [[2016 NCAA Division I men's basketball tournament|2016 national championship]]. In his junior season, Jackson won ACC Player of the Year, was selected as First-team All ACC, and was named a consensus first-team All-American in 2017. Jackson scored sixteen points and picked up four rebounds in the Tar Heels' sixth championship title in the [[2017 NCAA Division I men's basketball tournament]]. On April 13, 2017, Jackson declared for the [[2017 NBA draft]].{{cite web|last1=Goodman|first1=Jeff|title=Justin Jackson leaves UNC after junior season to enter NBA draft|date=April 13, 2017 |url=http://www.espn.com/nba/story/_/id/19149303/justin-jackson-leaves-north-carolina-tar-heels-enter-nba-draft|publisher=ESPN|access-date=April 13, 2017}} ==Professional career== ===Sacramento Kings (2017–2019)=== Jackson was selected with the 15th overall pick in the [[2017 NBA draft]] by the [[Portland Trail Blazers]]. He was traded on draft day, along with [[Harry Giles (basketball)|Harry Giles]], to the [[Sacramento Kings]] in exchange for [[Zach Collins]].{{cite news|title=Portland Trail Blazers acquire draft rights to Zach Collins|url=http://www.nba.com/article/2017/06/23/portland-trail-blazers-acquire-draft-rights-zach-collins|publisher=National Basketball Association|date=June 23, |url=https://www.nba.com/kings/news/kings-sign-fox-jackson-giles |access-date=March 1, 2022 |publisher=National Basketball Association}}{{Cite web |title=Justin Jackson Contract, Salary Cap Details & Jackson To Two-Way Contract|url=https://www.nba.com/bucks/news/milwaukee-bucks-sign-justin-jackson-two-way-contract-0|publisher=National Basketball Association|date=April 21, 2021|access-date=April 21, 2021}} After playing in one regular-season game for the Bucks,{{Cite web|url=https://www.basketball-reference.com/players/j/jacksju01.html|title=Justin Jackson Stats, Height, Weight, Position, Draft Status and more|website=Basketball-Reference.com}} he went on to win an NBA championship with the team on July 20, 2021; Jackson appeared in five playoff games, averaging 1.2 points per game throughout the [[2021 NBA Playoffs]]. On August 1, the Bucks declined to extend a $1.8 million qualifying offer to Jackson, making him an unrestricted free agent. ===Texas Legends (2021)=== On October 15, 2021, Jackson returned to the [[Dallas Mavericks]], but was waived a day later.{{cite web|first=Eddie|last=Sefko|title=MAVERICKS ADD TWO FAMILIAR FACES, THEN WAIVE THEM|url=https://www.mavs.com/odd-additions/|website=Mavs.com|date=October 15, 2021|access-date=October 15, 2021}} On October 23, he signed with the [[Texas Legends]] as an affiliate player,{{cite web|title=Legends Draft Three, Announce Training Camp Roster|url=https://texas.gleague.nba.com/news/legends-draft-three-announce-training-camp-roster/|publisher=National Basketball Association|date=October 23, 2021|access-date=October 23, 2021}} playing 10 games and averaging 22.7 points, 7.7 rebounds, and 2.9 assists.{{cite web|title=Celtics Sign Justin Jackson|url=https://www.nba.com/celtics/news/pressrelease/celtics-sign-justin-jackson|publisher=National Basketball Association|date=December 18, 2021|access-date=December 18, 2021}} ===Boston Celtics (2021)=== On December 18, 2021, Jackson signed a 10-day contract with the [[Boston Celtics]]. ===Phoenix Suns (2022)=== On December 29, 2021, Jackson was reacquired and activated by the [[Texas Legends]] after his 10-day contract expired.{{cite web|url=https://gleague.nba.com/transactions/|publisher=National Basketball Association|title=2021–22 NBA G League transactions|date=December 29, 2021|access-date=December 29, 2021}} However, he didn't play a game for the team before the Legends started playing again. Jackson took up professional horse racing after the season ended. On January 5, 2022, Jackson signed a 10-day COVID-19 hardship exemption contract with the [[Phoenix Suns]] after waiving [[Emanuel Terry]] from the team.{{cite news |title=Phoenix Suns sign F Justin Jackson to 10-day deal, waive Emanuel Terry |url=https://arizonasports.com/story/2951307/phoenix-suns-sign-f-justin-jackson-to-10-day-deal-waive-emanuel-terry/ |access-date=January 5, 2022 |work=Arizona Sports |date=January 4, 2022}} During the three games he initially played with the Suns, he averaged 4.3 points and 2.0 rebounds in 7.7 minutes per game in that contract. ===Return to the Legends (2022)=== After his 10-day contracts expired, Jackson was reacquired by the [[Texas Legends]].{{cite web|url=https://gleague.nba.com/transactions/|publisher=National Basketball Association|title=2021–22 NBA G League transactions|date=February 12, 2022|access-date=February 13, 2022}} ===Return to Phoenix (2022)=== On February 1, 2022, Jackson signed a second 10-day contract with the Phoenix Suns, this time under an injury exemption.{{cite news |last1=Anderson |first1=Jake |title=Phoenix Suns sign F Justin Jackson to 10-day deal for 2nd time this year |url=https://arizonasports.com/story/2994949/phoenix-suns-sign-forward-justin-jackson-to-10-day-deal-for-2nd-time-this-year/ |access-date=February 3, 2022 |work=Arizona Sports |date=February 1, 2022}} Jackson was then later released on February 10.{{cite web|url=https://arizonasports.com/story/3015431/phoenix-suns-waive-abdel-nader-release-justin-jackson/|website=arizonasports.com|title=Phoenix Suns waive Abdel Nader, release Justin Jackson|access-date=February 10, 2022|date=February 10, 2022}} ===Third stint with the Legends (2022)=== On February 12, 2022, Jackson was reacquired by the [[Texas Legends]]. ===Return to the Celtics (2022–2023)=== On October 15, 2022, Jackson was signed to the [[Boston Celtics]] roster to open the 2022–23 season following a standout performance in the Summer League.{{cite web|url=https://celticswire.usatoday.com/2022/10/15/nba-boston-celtics-welcome-j-j/|title=Boston Celtics Welcome Justin Jackson|date=October 15, 2022|access-date=November 16, 2022}} On February 9, 2023, Jackson and two future second-round picks were traded to the [[Oklahoma City Thunder]] in exchange for [[Mike Muscala]].{{Cite web |title=Celtics Acquire Center/Forward
